descriptions.adverb-particle-viewpoint-engineering: Use when a particle, adverb, clitic, or aspect marker changes how an event is understood without changing the event — 又/才/也/竟/还/只, ふと/ちらり/じっと, expectation, presupposition, deictic center, empathy — and the question is which reader stance each carrier produces; use for minimal-pair tests of attention, recurrence, threshold, and violated expectation in any language; carries the Japanese viewpoint tradition (ふと/じっと, 来る/行く, giving/receiving, zero-subject continuity) as a laboratory.
descriptions.camera-attention-engineering: Use when a scene’s vocabulary is acceptable but the reader sees it in the wrong order, distance, scale, or access path; when reveal, occlusion, observer movement, attention shifts, or “移步换景” matter more than ornament.
descriptions.character-motive: Use when a character feels flat, “three-dimensional” only because opposite traits were pasted together, or keeps changing personality to surprise the reader; use when a stable motive should generate unusual labels that later scenes repeatedly overturn; use when behavior needs a partially coherent model — durable motives plus habits, beliefs, misbeliefs, role performance, and an unexplained residual — instead of a compressible decision function.
descriptions.chinese-derived-event-geometry: Use when a passage can gain precision by treating verbs as event geometry: serial action, direction, result, temporary predicate coercion, role reassignment, or eventifying static properties into event consequences. Source tradition: Chinese, where these operations are cheap to see; includes a transfer procedure and a residue record for any target language with a natural carrier.
descriptions.corpus-convergence-audit: Use when many outputs, chapters, or corpus samples use different words but feel like the same writer — the same narrative operation skeleton under different vocabulary; use to detect operation-level convergence (sensory anomaly then mundane motive, object handoff, deleted explanation, motif return) that surface n-grams cannot catch.
descriptions.counterfactual-revision: Use when the user wants to know which local change actually improves or harms a passage, compare two revisions, test a suspected relation word, adjective, name, verb, particle, or metaphor, swap subject/object focus, or revise by controlled one-variable interventions rather than wholesale rewriting; this is the pack's shared experiment protocol — every layer has a canonical intervention.
descriptions.dialogue-voice: Use when dialogue or close interior narration sounds like the author, a therapist, HR, a critic, or a generic model instead of the actual speaker; use when age, profession, knowledge, local motive, or social register should constrain wording; use when a character's voice should be modeled as a cross-layer profile — preferred names, address terms, hedges, particles, sentence endings, relation markers, habitual metaphors, verb commitment, ellipsis, repair patterns.
descriptions.english-derived-motion-packaging: Use when manner, path, particles, prepositions, reveal, or field-of-view motion should be packed tightly into a clause. Source tradition: English, where manner+path packing is cheap to see; includes a transfer procedure and a residue record for any target language without forcing English phrasal-verb syntax.
descriptions.french-derived-motion-packaging: Use when path, manner, appearance, perception, or motion packaging should be separated before rewriting. Source tradition: French, where the path/manner/appearance hierarchy is easy to expose; includes a transfer procedure and a residue record for any target language without forcing French verb-framed syntax.
descriptions.knowledge-boundaries: Use when characters act on what they know, don't know, or misbelieve — and the narrative manages the gap between character knowledge, narrator knowledge, and reader knowledge; use for dramatic irony, concealment, disclosure, misrecognition, and the timing of what each party learns.
descriptions.literary-evals: Use when testing literary skills, prompts, rubrics, or repeated model outputs for trigger accuracy, causal understanding, counterexample handling, cross-language transfer, regression, or newly learned stock phrases rather than revising one passage only; use for the pack's per-skill trigger batteries (22 skills) and minimal-pair suites.
descriptions.literary-strategy-controller: Use when a revision plan is being executed over a longer passage and several local fixes are already in play — track the document state, compute marginal utility before each next operation, and avoid turning six individually correct local choices into one house style; use for state-dependent adaptation instead of randomization.
descriptions.literary-style-router: Use when a fiction-writing or revision request is broad, vague, or described only as “AI-like,” “flat,” “wooden,” “purple,” “not literary,” or “make it better,” and the actual failure mechanism has not yet been identified; routes in two stages — first the carrying layer, then the mechanism within it.
descriptions.metaphor-audit: Use when a metaphor, simile, analogy, or figurative comparison feels generic, ornamental, cliché, overlong, or interchangeable with thousands of objects; use when deciding whether a literal description is stronger than an image, or when a character's habitual metaphor is doing voice work; use before generating new metaphors — audit first, "no metaphor needed" is a valid verdict.
descriptions.naming-and-address-engineering: Use for a single naming act in one scene: the same person or object referred to in a way that changes the frame — 狗/野狗/那畜生/阿黄, 那个男人/老头/李叔/父亲/主任 — and the choice of name carries knowledge, social relation, emotional distance, or narrative alignment; use when renaming should happen because the frame changed, not for variety.
descriptions.narrator-intervention-abstraction-contro: Use when the narrator names emotions, states, or meanings too directly, concludes before the scene earns it, summarizes in a foreign register (staff report, therapy recap, retrospective memo, self-help), or when abstraction density and explicit state naming should be controlled; use for evidence policy — when to offer bounded concrete evidence instead of a psychological label.
descriptions.predicate-licensing-and-personification: Use when a noun carries a predicate its class normally cannot — 风追着他, 门犹豫了一下才开, 城市醒了, 雪把声音接住了 — and the question is whether the crossing earns its cost; use when personification or agentive coercion should be diagnosed as a recoverable boundary crossing, not praised or banned by taste.
descriptions.property-and-adjective-engineering: Use when adjectives feel decorative, piled up, or wrong in a way that is hard to name; use when a property is assigned by an adjective (or adverb, or attributive noun) and the question is what job the property does; classify before deleting or replacing — discriminative, state-bearing, evaluative, or affective adjectives fail and pay differently.
descriptions.relation-scaffolding: Use when fiction keeps stating edges between events, states, or propositions — causation, contrast, implication, relationship, process, meaning — that event order or syntax could carry; use for AI-flavored concept-link scaffolds (“并非A而是B,” “不仅而且,” “因此可以看出,” “某种意义上”) and beginner event-link chains (“然后…然后…”); also use when the user wants a frequency/context audit of Chinese function words or relation-heavy content words.
descriptions.sentence-pressure: Use when prose drags, chops, stacks qualifications, repeats without building, or varies sentence length mechanically; use when the real issue is the timing of information, uncertainty, release, interruption, or syntactic load; also use when rhythm is phonetic or prosodic — stress, breath, momentum, parallelism — rather than informational.
descriptions.social-naming-relation-maps: Use for the whole-work view of naming: names and address terms encoding a relationship's trajectory across a work, naming consistency, and the global map where single naming acts accumulate — who calls whom what, when it changes, and what the map says about the social structure; use for naming consistency, relation arcs (李叔→老李→李建国), and the global frame where local naming acts (see naming-and-address-engineering) accumulate into structure.
descriptions.verb-event-engineering: Use when a fiction sentence has weak, decorative, over-rare, morally overcommitted, or role-confusing verbs; when changing a predicate may alter agency, responsibility, causation, control, intention, duration, path, result, or the noun's role in the event; use when an event needs decomposition before any verb is replaced.
